pending_commit.commit_message: tast: Improve SSH's API to push files. SSH.PutTreeRename used to take the base directory in the local and remote host and files were specified in paths relative to the base directory. Assumption here was that we usually want to push files under a base directory, but it is not true today especially when a test bundle binary and local_test_runner are pushed at once. This CL changes the method to take just one map whose key is an absolute/relative path to a local file and value is an absolute path to a remote file. Since we no longer have concept of the base directory, the method is renamed from PutTreeRename to PutFiles. CHROMIUM: bluetooth/sco - Parse correct conn handle According to Core spec 5.4.3 HCI Synchronous Data Packets the Connection_Handle uses the first 12 bits of header. This change fixes the connection handle value. Otherwise if the succeeding 2 bits of packet status flag is set, it could result in connection look up failure and drop one SCO packet. BUG=chromium:980454 TEST=Test wideband speech headset, verify there's no error printed for 'SCO packet for unknown connection handle' Change-Id: I790068203e4444f39e835bb070c3d4cc38051c93 Signed-off-by: Hsin-Yu Chao <hychao@google.com> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1683384 Tested-by: Hsinyu Chao <hychao@chromium.org> Commit-Ready: Hsinyu Chao <hychao@chromium.org> Legacy-Commit-Queue: Commit Bot <commit-bot@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: En-Shuo Hsu <enshuo@google.com> Reviewed-by: Yoni Shavit <yshavit@chromium.org>

CHROMIUM: bluetooth/sco - Keep HCI SCO packet header in transparent mode According to Core spec 5.4.3 HCI Synchronous Data Packets, when erroneous data reporting feature is enabled, controller sets the packet status flag to indicate if data is intact in the payload. For wide band speech mode using voice_transparent settings, user space wants to know the value of packet status flag for packet loss concealment. We shall not strip the HCI SCO packet header in this case. BUG=chromium:980454 TEST=Apply CRAS patches and test WBS headset. Verified the erroneous data reporting is working fine by flagging lost/partial data. Change-Id: I07ed7d984913f3346c0b0d7efc2c283404110d49 Signed-off-by: Hsin-Yu Chao <hychao@google.com> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1683385 Tested-by: Hsinyu Chao <hychao@chromium.org> Commit-Ready: Hsinyu Chao <hychao@chromium.org> Legacy-Commit-Queue: Commit Bot <commit-bot@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: En-Shuo Hsu <enshuo@google.com> Reviewed-by: Yoni Shavit <yshavit@chromium.org>

ml: Get memory usage from proc/[pid]/status The previous code parses /proc/[pid]/totmaps to obtain the memory usage, but this is deprecated and has been removed upstream (crbug.com/979781). In the modification, we instead parse the /proc/[pid]/status and use VmRSS+VmSwap as the memory usage. The new method does not use the hand-coded indices so the result should be more robust. The new number reported will be a bit different from the previous one because it will include the shared memory. This should be fine because it is the relative sizes of the numbers that matter, rather the absolute values.
